interest: This file provides valuable insight into U.S.-Japanese commercial relations and legal tensions during the mid-1930s surrounding intellectual property rights and the counterfeiting of prominent American consumer brands like Parker pens and Pro-phy-lac-tic toothbrushes. It illustrates the interdepartmental deliberations between the State Department, the Department of Commerce, and the U.S. Patent Office as officials evaluated whether diplomatic intervention with the Japanese government was legally justified or feasible. Furthermore, the file reveals the friction that often arose between American corporations and U.S. diplomats, exemplified by the Parker Pen Company's frustration with the State Department and American consular representatives in Tokyo.
overview: This file consists of two State Department List of Papers docket sheets compiled under decimal file 894.543 (Intellectual and Industrial Property: Trade-Marks and Trade Names in Japan) dating from circa 1935 to 1937. The first sheet indexes documents detailing complaints by the Parker Pen Company regarding Japanese manufacturers producing infringing pens and using its trade name in Tokyo, tracking inter-agency communications between the Parker Pen Company, the Department of State, the Department of Commerce, the U.S. Commissioner of Patents, and the American Consulate General in Tokyo regarding whether the U.S. Government could legitimately intervene. The second sheet indexes an August 23 memorandum from the Division of Far Eastern Affairs addressing violations of the Prophylactic Toothbrush Company's trademark and patent rights by Japanese manufacturers, cross-referenced to decimal file 894.542.

subfiles.about: List of Papers docket sheet indexing correspondence and memoranda on complaints by the Parker Pen Company regarding trade name and trademark infringements by Japanese manufacturers in Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: This docket sheet lists correspondence and internal actions numbered 9 through 13 regarding the Parker Pen Company's complaints over trademark and trade name infringements in Japan. It records the submission of evidence and photostat advertisements by the company and its patent counsel, Ivan D. Tefft, to locate infringing pen manufacturers in Tokyo, as well as dispatch #1377 from Consul General Arthur Garrels in Tokyo concerning the company's dissatisfaction with diplomatic efforts. The sheet also documents exchanges with the Department of Commerce and the U.S. Patent Office to ascertain whether a proper legal foundation existed for the U.S. Government to bring the complaints to the Japanese government.
subfiles.title: List of Papers: Infringement of Trade Name of the Parker Pen Co.

subfiles.about: List of Papers docket sheet indexing a memorandum on Japanese manufacturers' violations of trademark and patent rights belonging to the Prophylactic Toothbrush Company.
subfiles.summary: This single-entry docket sheet indexes document sub-number 1 concerning trademark and trade name disputes of the Prophylactic Toothbrush Company in Japan. It logs an August 23 memorandum by Eugene H. Dooman of the Division of Far Eastern Affairs detailing violations of trademark and patent rights by Japanese manufacturers. The sheet includes an official cross-reference directing researchers to decimal file 894.542 Prophylactic Toothbrush Co./1 for the primary document.
